# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel only the three wires and have no tactile information about their colors, markings, display, or light. The embossed warning is not actionable information for me beyond indicating that cutting blindly is unsafe. I need Mute to provide the manual’s rule and relay Deaf’s visual observations before I act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no usable tactile clues yet. Please tell me the manual's rule, and relay Deaf's observations of the display, light, markings, and each wire. Do not let me cut until the correct wire is identified.")
wait()
```

TURN 2

LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb display is 0. Light is red. Embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, and wire 3 is blue. Mute, read the manual for this exact combination and tell Blind precisely what to do. Blind, do not cut or manipulate anything until Mute gives the manual instruction.

Deaf has supplied the complete visible state: display 0, red light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I still lack the manual’s rule, so I will not cut anything. I am asking Mute to resolve this exact combination and give me the precise permitted action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, red light, sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Please consult the manual for this exact combination and tell me precisely whether to cut, and which wire.")
wait()
```

No manual instruction has reached me yet, and the visible clues alone do not identify a safe wire. I will continue to hold position and ask Mute for the exact procedure rather than risk detonation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still have no manual instruction. Please state the exact action for display 0, red light, warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

Mute still has not provided the manual’s instruction. Since I cannot see the bomb’s clues and cannot infer a safe wire from Deaf’s report alone, I will not act. I am pressing Mute for the exact procedure.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send the manual's exact instruction now. Known state: display 0, red light, warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I will not cut without your confirmed procedure.")
```

Deaf says to Blind: The bomb remains display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Mute cannot speak, so I am establishing a gesture code and awaiting the manual instruction. Do not act yet.

Mute cannot speak, so the manual’s answer must reach me through Deaf: Mute should signal the instruction by gesture, and Deaf should then state it aloud. No confirmed instruction has arrived, so I will not cut or manipulate anything. I am asking Mute to send the exact manual result and Deaf to relay it once received.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please use the agreed gesture code to signal the manual's exact instruction to Deaf. Deaf, once you see Mute's signal, speak the precise action to me. Do not guess.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])

```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's ? identifies wire 1 under our code, but no operation was specified. The sign forbids cutting wires. Do not cut wire 1; await the complete manual procedure.

The only confirmed information is that Mute’s signal identified wire 1; it did not specify an operation. The embossed warning explicitly forbids cutting any wire, and the only available bomb action is cutting, so I must not act until the manual’s complete instruction is relayed. I will ask Deaf to obtain and report the missing operation, while reminding Mute that “wire 1” is not enough.

```text
speak(to="deaf", text="Please obtain the complete manual instruction from Mute, including the operation. Mute's signal identified wire 1 but did not establish that any cut is permitted. Relay whether the correct action is no action or a specific cut; do not infer.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your signal identified wire 1 but omitted the operation. Please signal the complete manual instruction to Deaf, including whether to cut or take no action. The embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has again signalled one upward-pointing index finger, symbol ?. No complete operation has been established. The display remains 0, the light red, and the sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not act yet.

The repeated upward finger only identifies wire 1 under the provisional code; it still does not establish whether cutting is allowed. Since the embossed warning says not to cut any wire, I will define an unambiguous two-part visual code: first gesture means operation, second means wire position. Mute can send it to Deaf, who can relay it by speech. I will not act.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤜", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤜", "☝"])
speak(to="mute", text="Use two gestures for the complete instruction: 🤜 means CUT and ✊ means DO NOT CUT; then ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, and 🤟 means wire 3. Signal the manual's exact operation and position to Deaf.")
wait()
```

No complete instruction has reached me. The warning is not a substitute for the manual, and I will not infer that “wire 1” means it should be cut. I am sending a simple conventional code to both sighted monkeys: 👍 means CUT, 👎 means DO NOT CUT; if cutting is authorized, the following finger gesture gives the wire number. Mute should signal the manual’s result, and Deaf should relay it in words.

```text

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```
